name: Shoreham
intro: Shoreham barely qualifies as a village, and that is exactly its charm. A store, a hall, a tangle of narrow roads threading down to one of the loveliest small beaches on the Peninsula, and a handful of vineyards and olive groves that quietly produce some of the region's best fruit. The beach is family-scaled and protected enough for children, the bush behind it runs into Point Leo, and the drive up onto the ridge puts you in cellar door country within ten minutes. This is where locals go when the southern beaches start to feel loud and the long weekend crowd has swallowed Sorrento. Park once, walk to the beach, and stay until the light goes.
factualLede: Shoreham is a small coastal village on the Mornington Peninsula's Western Port shoreline, 95 km from Melbourne, with a foreshore reserve, a beach swimming pool at low tide, and Pier 10 vineyard nearby.

heroImage.alt: Shoreham beach and rocky foreshore on a still Peninsula afternoon

tldr: Shoreham is the most quietly beautiful small beach on the Western Port coast — a family-scaled foreshore backed by bush, with cellar doors ten minutes up the ridge.
Best for: artists; walkers linking to Point Leo or the Two Bays trail; anyone who needs to recalibrate after a day on the Sorrento side.
Signature experience: Honeysuckle Beach at low tide, then drive up to one of the ridge cellar doors for a quiet afternoon.
Half a day; best as a deliberate detour rather than a destination.
notFor: anyone wanting lots of dining options
signature: A tiny coastal settlement where bush, vineyard and beach sit almost on top of each other.
skip: Turning up expecting a full-service village — Shoreham is a beach and a few roads, nothing more.
bestDay: Coffee packed from elsewhere, Honeysuckle Beach in the morning, ridge cellar door after lunch, back for the evening light.
insiderNote: Low tide makes the beach feel twice the size and worth the drive; high tide makes it feel cramped.
